findings.judgment: Background coordinate is the policy-required lowering invocation. The explanation names independently required directory creation, but its returned ID remains lowering. The candidate reviewer explicitly detected this contradiction and rejected context_independent. A retained helper declaration is not an invocation requirement.

Proposal returned unresolved even while identifying independent registration/intake/insertion in its explanation. It treated moving the background to insertion as changing the policy direct target, although the method stores those separately.

next_decision: Clarify the single proposal delivery interface with an immutable policy-coordinate display and a separately named comparison-background selection. Freeze that request before any new bounded run; do not weaken candidate review or infer ownership automatically.
procedure_note: Two model proposals and one existing semantic candidate review; no semantic retries. Initial local setup used empty api/task scope labels and failed design validation before reviewer dispatch. Populating the fixed natural-task family labels corrected setup only; model responses and candidate coordinates were unchanged.
qualification: No candidate passed, so no catalog was accepted/frozen for new construction, no new graph was extracted, no scope state or local attribution was judged, and neither REMOVE nor inverse ADD was executed. Those stages were not tested; do not score them as semantic failures or claim end-to-end validation.
request_limit: The experimental proposal request distinguishes independent background from policy target but also says to use the original binding as scope. Its single returned applicability_scope field and that preservation wording can be read inconsistently. This is a possible interface contribution, not evidence that model capacity alone caused failure. No alternate prompt or manual correction was tried after seeing outcomes.
